key_terms: The reviewable record of what was built, the bounded input, the expected result and which stages were only parsed, compiled or configured.
A stated, source-bound result that a capstone run must reproduce exactly before it counts as passing.
A course workshop whose actual components have run and been recorded in its qualification ledger, unlike one that is only prepared.
Starting, retaining and destroying only the capstone's own labeled resources, with destruction requiring explicit confirmation.

worked_examples.title: Hash the sources a dossier depends on
worked_examples.interpretation: Each line pairs a SHA-256 digest with a file name. The receipt from batch_snapshot.py already embeds its own source hash; comparing that value with this command shows the reviewed code is the code that ran. A reviewer who gets a different digest should treat every result in the dossier as unverified until the mismatch is explained.

worked_examples.title: Check that the dossier states its boundaries
worked_examples.code:
receipt = {
    "passed": True,
    "fresh_catalog_readback": True,
    "wrong_catalog_rejected": True,
    "direct_spark_or_iceberg_datafusion_connector_qualified": False,
}
required = ["passed", "fresh_catalog_readback", "wrong_catalog_rejected"]
missing = [key for key in required if receipt.get(key) is not True]
print("missing:", missing, "declared unsupported:", [k for k, v in receipt.items() if v is False])
worked_examples.interpretation: The fields come from the integration receipt. A good dossier states both what passed and what was not qualified; here the Spark connector route is declared false rather than omitted. A reviewer can then see at once that the capstone proves the Iceberg, Arrow and DataFusion path and makes no claim about Spark.

evidence: A selected actual supported path with independent source/result/failure/lifecycle evidence; combined topologies and prepared native-server alternatives require separate acceptance and are not inferred from component tests.
